en: The Sūtra on the Names of the Eight Classes of Buddhas Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Indian Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was traveling through Vaiśālī at the Āmrapālī Grove, together with a great assembly.
The Master was accompanied by a multitude: one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus and an incalculable number of bodhisattvas.

At that time, there was the son of an elder named Shan-zuo (Sujāta), who came out from the city and went to the Nyagrodha Grove. Arriving at the place where the World-Honored One was, he prostrated at His feet, circumambulated Him three times to the right, and withdrew to stand to one side.
With palms joined, he addressed the Buddha: "I wish to ask a question. If the Great Sage would grant me leave, I would venture to speak."
The Buddha said to Kāla:
"Ask whatever you wish; the Tathāgata shall explain it to you in full detail.
Having been granted permission, Kāla addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O God among Gods, are there indeed Buddhas who, having practiced their original vows, have attained perfect enlightenment and now presently expound the Way of the sutras?"

Great Sage, we pray that you will proclaim the names of all Buddhas; having heard them, we shall uphold them, wear them upon our crowns, receive their teachings, prostrate and take refuge in them, and proclaim their meritorious achievements. Thus, we shall no longer encounter various difficulties, nor shall we fall into the three miserable realms. Upon hearing the names of the Buddhas, neither humans nor non-humans shall find an opportunity to harm us. If we are involved with government officials, by reciting the names of the Buddhas, none shall be able to wrongfully seize what belongs to us. Furthermore, our nature shall become firm and strong, free from cowardice or weakness; we shall attain peace and victory. Moreover, when entering battle, blades shall not wound our bodies and arrows shall not penetrate us. Yakṣas, various ghosts, devas, nāgas, and spirits shall not dare to harass us, and lions, tigers, wolves, wild beasts, and venomous insects shall be unable to cause us harm.
The Buddha told Kalyāṇakārī:
"Listen attentively!
Reflect upon it well!"
"I shall now explain for you the means of protection that removes calamities, so that you may be free from fear and attain peace.
Thereupon, Sujāta received the instruction and listened.
The Buddha said:
"To the east of here, there is a Buddha named Upaśāntacittarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides and expounds the Dharma; his world is called Yaśaskīrti."

"Furthermore, in the eastern direction there is a Buddha named Dṛḍhavīryaprasaragatārthasiddhi Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there preaching the Dharma; his world is called Anabhibhūta."
"Furthermore, to the east of this buddha-field, there is a Buddha named Avalokita-guṇa-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides and teaches the Dharma; his world is named Kṣema."

"Furthermore, to the east of this buddha-field, there is a Buddha named Maitreyaśrīpraśāntamūrdha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides and preaches the Dharma; his world is called Avyāpāda."

"Furthermore, to the east of this buddha-field, there is a Buddha named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Supreme Leader of True Nature, who currently resides and expounds the Dharma; the world is named Abandoned Staff."

"Furthermore, to the east of this buddha-field, there is a Buddha named Nianshēngchēngshàngshǒu (Sattvānusmṛti-pramukha) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides and expounds the Dharma. His world is called Chìshèngshǒu (Jvalanottama)."

"Furthermore, in the eastern direction there is a Buddha named Vyūhaśikhara-abhyudgata-sumeru Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently present preaching the Dharma; his world is called Rucira-jvalita-śikhara."

"Furthermore, to the east of this buddha-field, there is a Buddha named Jina-vikhyāta-agrasena Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides and teaches the Dharma; his world is called Priya."

"Suppose there is someone who hears from afar the names of the Tathāgatas of the eastern quarter; having received these names of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, they reverently uphold them, contemplate them well, and cherish them in their hearts, reciting, chanting, and reading them. Even though the Buddhas' virtues of precepts, wisdom, and the root of the Path are equal;

and even though the adornments of their lands are pure and extraordinary, standing alone without peer, free from dust and defilement, free from the hardships of female impurity, free from the afflictions of the five turbidities, free from the calamities of the three miserable realms, and free from sand, gravel, stones, thorns, ditches, and pits."
The Buddha said: "Excellent!

If there are those who can uphold and proclaim the names of these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, far and wide; who rise from sleep during the first watch of the night to practice walking meditation, praising, chanting, and reciting the names of these Buddhas; and who, during the middle and final watches of the night, arise and dwell with a single-minded focus, abandoning what is unprofitable and reflecting upon their increased cultivation—such practitioners will advance daily in virtue and merit, never suffering any decline."
The Buddha told Suvikrānta:

"You should take delight in this sutra of the names of the eight Buddhas. The Buddhas teach this Dharma to sons of noble family; you should cherish it in your heart and not forget or abandon it. If you cultivate it diligently at once, you shall immediately behold eight thousand Buddhas."

Having thus heard the holy instruction, Kalyāṇakārin took a precious flower worth eight thousand taels of gold and scattered it as an offering over the World-Honored One; he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and then withdrew to sit.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, was present in that assembly and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Indeed, O Great Sage!
I have already received the names of these eight Buddhas; I recite and read them, holding them within my heart."

O God among Gods, I shall diligently apply myself with vigor to practice and uphold the names of these Buddhas of the eight assemblies; I shall contemplate and focus my mind upon them without ceasing even for the duration of eating or breathing, holding them in high esteem and reverence as the unsurpassed treasure.
The Buddha told Śakra, Lord of Devas:
"For this reason, when the devas and asuras are engaged in battle, if there should be fear, Kauśika, you should maintain mindfulness so that you may be without dread."
Why is this? If someone were to praise and extol the names of the Tathāgatas through the eight classes of scriptures, they would be proclaiming the karma of fearlessness;
one who declares the names of the Tathāgatas' scriptures shall not encounter the calamities of affliction, feverish distress, or various misfortunes.
If one can manifest and transmit the essentials of the sutras containing the names of all Tathāgatas, then one proclaims an era of great peace and abundance;
if one can transmit the names of the sutras of all Buddhas, then one proclaims tranquility and the removal of great calamities;
if one can transmit the names of the sutras of all Buddhas, then one proclaims the practice of silent, peaceful meditation.
If one transmits the names of the various Buddhas' sutras, one will be free from all countless fears;

if one can transmit this Sutra of the Names of the Various Buddhas, one will be peaceful in dreams and joyful upon waking, and shall not fear government officials, water, fire, or bandits. Enemies and creditors will naturally avoid one, and ghosts, spirits, rākṣasas, yāksas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, and those who cast curses will all dare not confront one.

If one enters mountains, hills, valleys, or desolate paths, plundering robbers will naturally not appear, and lions, tigers, wolves, bears, badgers, snakes, and vipers will all naturally shrink back and hide away.

Why is this so? Because the supreme virtue of the Buddhas exceeds Mount Sumeru, their wisdom surpasses the rivers and seas, and their insight transcends empty space; they walk alone through the three realms with none able to equal them, and there are none throughout the ten directions who do not receive their deliverance.

When the Buddha had spoken thus, the elder Svastyāyanī, Śakra Devendra, the assembly of bhikṣus, and all those present—including gods, nāgas, asuras, and worldly humans—rejoiced upon hearing the sutra; they paid homage and withdrew.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Names of the Eight Classes of Beings.
